channel.description: Latest articles from The Garden Island (thegardenisland.com)

item.title: Officials warn of potentially inclement weather into next week
item.description: LIHUE — County of Kauai officials are urging the public to be vigilant due to potential severe weather conditions beginning this weekend and continuing into next week.

item.title: Waimea girls advance at the Division II state girls basketball championships
item.description: HILO — Waimea High School, seeded No. 2 in the Division II state girls basketball championships, beat unseeded Mid Pacific Institute, 52-39, on Thursday to advance to the semifinals today at the Hilo Civic Center on Hawaii Island.

item.title: Hawaii legislative bills advance to unmask ICE agents
item.description: The first of several Hawaii legislative bills that would unmask federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents was met with concerns Tuesday from the Honolulu Police Department and state Department of Law Enforcement that backup officers from their departments also could be identified while supporting local undercover operations.

item.title: SBA programs for native businesses face scrutiny
item.description: The Native Hawaiian Organizations Association is urging President Donald Trump’s administration to distinguish between “isolated allegations” about the Small Business Administration’s program aimed at developing native-run businesses and its success expanding economic opportunity, as U.S. Rep. Ed Case calls for a formal review.

item.title: Hawaii lawmaker looks to ban popular ‘prediction market’ wagering
item.description: Ahead of Gov. Josh Green’s annual State of the State address last week, online bettors placed $448,667 in “prediction market” wagers on whether he would say phrases that included “affordable,” “affordability,” “mainland,” “cost of living,” “aloha,” “kauhale,” “housing,” “health care,” “tourism” and “volcano” as part of an online gambling phenomenon that would be prohibited under House Bill 2198.

item.title: Bezos donation boosts Lahainaluna scholarships and wildfire research
item.description: Cecelia Steiner was preparing to start her senior year at Lahainaluna High School — serving as student body president and planning for college — when the Aug. 8, 2023, wildfire tore through Lahaina the day before classes were set to begin.

item.title: Gabbard rejects whistleblower claims
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard on Saturday disputed claims by lawmakers that she sought to block Congress from accessing a whistleblower complaint, saying she took “immediate action” once notified of the need to provide security guidance for its release.

item.title: Memorial honors Hawaii soldiers aboard Army ship torpedoed off Big Island in 1942
item.description: A new Big Island memorial honors Hawaii-born soldiers who were on the U.S. Army Transport Royal T. Frank when it was torpedoed by a Japanese submarine on Jan. 28, 1942, in waters off North Kohala.

item.title: Hawaii lawmakers seek ban on surfboard wax made with ‘forever chemicals’
item.description: A drive in Hawaii over the past few years to rid “forever chemicals” from consumer products including food packaging, cosmetics and clothing has a new focus this year: surfboard wax.

item.title: Hawaii man sentenced to life for trying to assassinate Trump
item.description: FORT PIERCE, Fla. — Ryan Routh, the former Hawaii resident accused of hiding in the bushes of a Florida golf course with a semi-automatic rifle to try to assassinate Donald Trump less than two months before the 2024 U.S. election that returned him to the presidency, was sentenced by a judge today to life in prison.
